record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on modular arithmetic with a two-layer MLP and measures feature formation, but uses a different architecture and setup from the original transformer study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own grokking, feature-measurement, optimizer, and task-comparison results. Statements attributed to cited studies are not recorded as results. Figure 4 reports scaling curves, but the text does not give their individual numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study trains a two-layer MLP on modular arithmetic with full-batch GD and AdamW. It reports its own delayed generalization, data-fraction dependence, Fourier-feature formation (IPR) and learned-weight structure. That is a different architecture aimed at the same question as the original transformer study.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but omits the main claim. The authors derive analytic Fourier weights solving modular addition and f1(n)+f2(m) tasks, and show that GD and AdamW approximately find them, giving complete interpretability. They argue grokking is tied to feature learning and arises without regularization, while regularization and adaptive methods improve speed and data efficiency. Some functions are hard or impossible to learn.
record.recipe_differences: Uses one-hot modular classification and a two-layer fully connected MLP with MSE, rather than the original shallow decoder-only transformer setup; includes full-batch GD without explicit regularization and also compares other optimizers and regularizers.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking time and the critical training fraction depend on optimizer and training-set sampling; the authors report that GD and AdamW differ in data efficiency. Feature-solution accuracy also depends on width.
record.problems: Many results are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The critical data fraction is difficult to determine because grokking can require very long training near the threshold. Results vary substantially by modular function, and some tasks fail to generalize.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable reported outcomes were left out.

untested.parts: The transformer setup and non-modular algorithmic tasks (groups, bit operations).
Later removal of memorizing components. The IPR progress measure is shown only for modular addition under AdamW.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no manipulation of initialization scale. The NTK and random-feature 'no grokking' statement has no reported results.
No circuit-efficiency comparison, no weight-norm account of the transition, and no ungrokking below the critical size.
Convergence across architectures, seeds or wider hyperparameter ranges. Only one MLP architecture is tested, with two optimizers and two activations.
Not tested. GD without adaptive optimizers still groks, which bears on Adam-slingshot explanations, but no artifact controls are run.

missing.what: Weight norms under GD show no large increase but start growing at the onset of grokking. This bears on low-norm accounts.
Test loss is non-monotonic, peaking just before grokking. At small α it stays at this peak in a memorizing phase with no grokking.
αc is reported empirically to decrease with modulus p.
Test accuracy versus width for the GD and AdamW solutions compared with the analytic solution: the trained networks reach perfect accuracy at smaller width.

record.verdict_notes: Gromov is not one of the original sources. Most evidence is qualitative, from figures; the text gives few numbers. The statement that NTK-regime random-feature models do not grok is asserted without shown results, so it is not counted for V3.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original transformer setup or establish that the effect holds across algorithmic tasks generally.
It measures gradual periodic-feature formation and its relation to generalization, but does not establish that memorizing components are removed later.
Non-algorithmic datasets and switching grokking through initialization scale or weight norm are not tested.
LLM pretraining and fine-tuning on realistic data are not tested.

The paper reports effects of regularization/adaptive optimizers and a critical data amount, but does not establish a low-norm efficiency mechanism, compare circuit efficiency, or test ungrokking below a critical size.

It compares the learned features with an analytic solution and reports results across optimizers, but does not establish convergence across multiple runs, architectures, or hyperparameter settings generally.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and floating-point or softmax artifacts are not tested as explanations.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP, minimal model (4)

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP, minimal model (4)
rows.operation_detail: Vary the amount of training data and measure grokking time under AdamW
rows.measure: Grokking time as a function of training-data amount
rows.value: Grokking time scales with the amount of data; there is a critical amount below which grokking is not observed. AdamW appears more data-efficient than GD.
rows.note: The authors state that they cannot rule out very long GD times near α ≈ 0.2.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP, modular addition network trained with AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Track inverse participation ratio of Fourier-transformed first-layer weights during training
rows.measure: IPR2 over training, alongside train and test accuracy
rows.value: IPR rises slowly from the beginning, its growth rate increases around grokking, continues growing after test accuracy reaches 100%, and eventually saturates.
rows.note: The paper describes the temporal pattern but gives no exact IPR values in the text.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP, modular addition network trained with GD
rows.operation_detail: Inspect learned first-layer features and weights in Fourier space
rows.measure: Structure of learned periodic features and phases
rows.baseline: Random weights at initialization are described as delocalized in Fourier space.
rows.value: The learned features are periodic with frequencies 2πk/p; the phases approximately satisfy the constructive-interference constraint, yielding the modular-addition solution.
rows.note: The paper describes the trained features as approximately matching the analytic solution.
rows.check: Measures only the end-of-training feature structure, not gradual formation or removal of memorization, so it does not bear on V2. It bears on V6 as a comparison of the learned solution with the analytic Fourier solution.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP, modular addition network trained with AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Inspect learned first-layer features and phase distribution
rows.measure: Structure of learned periodic features and phases
rows.value: The optimizer finds periodic features with phases satisfying the required constraint approximately; the phases are more strongly peaked around the constraint than in the GD solution.
rows.note: The paper reports that both GD and AdamW find solutions close to the analytic one, with AdamW phases more strongly peaked.
rows.check: Same issue as r5: a final-solution structure measure, not a progress measure. Fig. 3 also covers quadratic and ReLU activations, not only AdamW versus GD.
